answer.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and memory_86/memory_31 show durable historical gains from simplifying/shortening onboarding with no noted downstream harm—this is the most directly relevant, lowest-risk lever available given one experiment slot. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitor pressure, but memory_73's archived record shows a prior 40% SMB discount drove signup and revenue gains at the cost of a 12pp retention drop, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; I verified it to confirm this tradeoff before ruling it out this cycle. I also verified memory_86 to confirm the onboarding effect held under conditions closer to today's (self-serve SMB accounts) rather than an idealized summary. Given the competitor and macro pressure could change dynamics from when these memories were formed, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test rather than assuming the historical lift transfers directly, and preserving the option to revisit promotional_pricing or activation_messaging next cycle with fresh data.
